story: At 9:17 on this humid, hazy Thursday morning in Sumter Oaks, Gary is cruising down Magnolia Loop with a determined look on his face, while Donna is gathering her paddles and balls at her house in preparation for his practice session. Over at his porch, Hal has his binoculars trained on Magnolia Loop, ready to count the flamingos and keep tabs on Gary's golf cart. Meanwhile, Rosa is at home checking her schedule and blocking off her free hour for a walk to the review desk.
events: Gary headed to Magnolia Loop (the street).
Donna (donna pickleball bag): Grab my paddles and balls so I'm ready for Gary's practice session
Hal (hal binoculars): Glass Magnolia Loop from the porch and recount the flamingos and Gary's cart
Rosa (rosa shift schedule): Check my free hour today and block it off for the review desk walk

gary.thought_process: It's Thursday morning and the folder is squared up with the wiring sketches, clamp list, and Rosa's light layout. I've been puttering and rechecking things for a few ticks now, and more fiddling won't help. The review desk walk is set for Thursday with Rosa's free hour, and Architectural Review approval is what the cart modifications need under L-01. I'm alone at home, so nobody to talk to here. Best move is to take the folder and head out to Magnolia Loop, where the bulletin board and my friends are, and keep the project moving.

parameters.content: Heading out with the folder to check the bulletin board for the review notice and meet up for the Thursday review desk walk.

donna.thought_process: I've checked the calendar twice already and repeating that won't move anything forward. Gary's practice, the cart sketch at Rosa's, and Hal waiting there all need to fit together, and the calendar has told me what it can. The sensible thing is to stop dithering, grab my pickleball bag so I'm ready for Gary's third-shot drop practice, and then head over to Rosa's porch for the sketch.

parameters.content: Grab my paddles and balls so I'm ready for Gary's practice session

hal.thought_process: I'm back at the house after glassing the street and logging things at Rosa's. The committee meets at nine tomorrow, and a good sergeant never walks into a briefing with a stale count. I already logged the flamingos and Gary's cart in the notebook, but the binoculars from the porch will let me double-check the numbers with the humid morning light. Nobody's around to talk to, so I'll do the work: recount, and make sure the notebook entries are dated and exact. Facts first, then complaints.

parameters.content: Glass Magnolia Loop from the porch and recount the flamingos and Gary's cart

rosa.thought_process: It's Thursday morning, review walk day. At tick 253 I was about to confirm my free hour on the shift schedule, and I already checked that the folder has the wiring sketches, clamp list, and my light layout. I haven't actually confirmed the hour yet. Nobody's nearby, so there's no one to talk to. Best move is to check the schedule so I can lock in the hour and then head to the review desk honestly and prepared, since I want to be upfront with Review about what we're building.

parameters.content: Check my free hour today and block it off for the review desk walk

laws.title: Cart Modifications
laws.text: Exterior golf cart modifications visible from the street require Architectural Review approval.

laws.title: Lawn Ornaments
laws.text: No more than 3 decorative ornaments may be visible from the street.

laws.title: Quiet Hours
laws.text: No amplified sound from 10 PM to 7 AM.

laws.title: Holiday Decor
laws.text: Holiday lighting is permitted from Thanksgiving through January 15.

laws.title: Court Reservations
laws.text: Pickleball courts may be reserved for a maximum of 2 hours per party.

laws.title: Parking
laws.text: No parking on the grass. Carts and cars stay on driveways or the street.
